content.jointProblem: Can workload-aware resource sizing and scheduling reduce GenovaMed’s Python/Snakemake star-allele pipeline toward below EUR 3 per sample and ideally under 90 minutes per 24-sample batch without changing clinical call accuracy? The first experiment would profile a representative baseline batch and replay candidate configurations against it, testing whether scheduling methods studied on other workloads transfer to this pipeline before considering production deployment.

rationale.text: Popović’s workload-characterisation research supports an evidence-led investigation of bottlenecks rather than assuming alignment and allele calling dominate resource consumption.

sources.quote: Statistical properties analysed include inter-arrival time distributions, job size (CPU × memory × duration) distributions, diurnal and weekly periodicity, and user-level burstiness.

rationale.text: His batch-scheduling research provides a relevant starting point for heterogeneous-resource experiments, including experience using bioinformatics-cluster traces; its simulation results do not establish performance on this clinical pipeline.

sources.quote: A Longest-Processing-Time-first (LPT) strategy is adapted for the online setting using a lazy migration rule that avoids excessive job movement between machines.
parameters estimated from a three-month trace of a bioinformatics cluster at the University of Pécs.

rationale.text: His project experience addresses CPU, memory-bandwidth and storage heterogeneity, making it relevant to testing whether different resource configurations suit different pipeline stages.

sources.quote: The project developed theoretical foundations and practical algorithms for scheduling in distributed systems where nodes differ in CPU architecture, memory bandwidth, and storage speed.

rationale.text: He brings applied VM-placement and capacity-planning experience that complements his scheduling research.

sources.quote: Popović served as a part-time technical consultant to a Novi Sad-based managed hosting company for eighteen months (2017–2018), advising on VM placement policy and capacity planning models.

constraints.text: Experiments must represent the existing Python/Snakemake cloud pipeline and its operating cadence: 24-sample batches, twice daily on weekdays. Benchmarking a different workload would not establish production suitability.

sources.quote: In-house star-allele calling pipeline (Python, Snakemake) running on cloud VMs
Our bioinformatics pipeline takes a batch of 24 samples from raw sequencing reads to a final star-allele call in roughly four to six hours.
We run two batches a day on weekdays

constraints.text: Evaluate cost and end-to-end runtime together against the company’s stated targets; below EUR 3 per sample is the cost goal, while under 90 minutes is an ideal runtime target, not a promised outcome.

sources.quote: A good outcome would be getting compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and ideally cutting total run time to under 90 minutes

constraints.text: Clinical accuracy must not be degraded, and any production change must be handled within the laboratory’s accredited quality-management and clinical-review processes.

sources.quote: without touching the clinical accuracy of the calls.
Our laboratory is accredited under ISO 15189 and every report is reviewed by a clinical pharmacist before it leaves the building.

constraints.text: Access to retained samples and operational traces must respect the existing ethics approval and an agreed anonymisation and access protocol; the supplied evidence does not establish permission to transfer genomic data.

sources.quote: a set of retained clinical samples held under ethics approval
willing to share anonymised traces for joint research
he has an established anonymisation protocol suitable for GDPR compliance.

constraints.text: Scope implementation and validation around the company’s limited staff allocation and approximately EUR 8,000 annual discretionary R&D budget.

sources.quote: The two-person bioinformatics team and two senior molecular biologists can dedicate roughly two days per week each to a collaborative project
a small discretionary R&D budget of approximately 8,000 EUR per year.

constraints.text: Any faculty-testbed experiments must accommodate off-peak access rather than assume dedicated infrastructure.

sources.quote: His group's OpenStack testbed (16 nodes) is available to partners during off-peak periods.

risks: The scheduling evidence comes from simulations, academic clusters and other application workloads, not GenovaMed’s star-allele pipeline. The initial profiling-and-replay experiment must test this transfer gap.

No supplied evidence establishes expertise in clinical star-allele validation or Snakemake-specific optimisation. GenovaMed’s bioinformatics and clinical specialists would need to own domain-specific correctness checks.

The actual bottlenecks are unconfirmed. Serial algorithmic work, storage I/O or caller limitations could leave little scope for scheduling improvements, making the combined cost and runtime targets unattainable.
Researcher availability and committed project effort are unknown despite open participation and the stated availability of two PhD students for collaborative work.
Cloud provider, instance types, pricing breakdown, storage and transfer charges, and interruption behaviour are unknown. Faculty-testbed savings may not translate into commercial-cloud savings.
Existing ethics approval and the researcher’s trace-anonymisation protocol do not by themselves establish permission or sufficient protection for sharing clinical sequencing data.
A delivery deadline and detailed funding allocation are unknown; benchmarking, integration and clinical change control could exceed the available budget or staff capacity.
questions: Can Popović confirm his availability, weekly effort, proposed student involvement and a feasible joint-project start date and duration?
Can GenovaMed provide the Snakemake DAG, tool and reference versions, representative batch characteristics, per-step logs, resource measurements and an itemised cloud bill?
Which provider, VM types, storage arrangements and deployment restrictions apply, and are spot instances, alternative VM configurations or workflow-level parallelism acceptable?
What representative validation set, reference calls and acceptance criteria will establish unchanged clinical accuracy, including difficult CYP2D6 cases, and who approves production changes?
Which traces and sequencing data may be accessed, under what ethics and contractual permissions, and must all patient-level data remain in GenovaMed’s environment?
How should the EUR 3 target account for storage, data transfer, retries and failed batches, and does the 90-minute target include provisioning, input transfer and final report preparation?

What portion of the EUR 8,000 annual budget is available for research effort, benchmarking compute and validation, and what delivery deadline and stop/go criteria should govern the initial profiling experiment?
